transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, I guess what finally made me come in is that I just keep forgetting basic adult things. It's gotten really bad. Like, I forget to pay my bills, I forget to return emails for job interviews, I miss appointments... I just can't seem to follow through on regular errands. It's really starting to cost me real opportunities, and I just need to figure out what's going on.
Would you say you've struggled with this kind of forgetfulness and follow-through since you were a kid, or is this a new pattern that's developed more recently?

It's definitely not new. It's been like this since I was a kid. Um, even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright, but I was constantly losing my worksheets. I'd rush through directions without really reading them, and I was always talking out of turn. And my desk... it was always so messy that I literally couldn't find my assignments when it was time to turn them in. So yeah, it's been a problem for as long as I can remember.
Besides the forgetfulness and disorganization, do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or like you have to keep moving, or find yourself talking excessively or interrupting others?

Yeah, definitely. Um, especially when I have to sit still for things. Like, if I'm in an interview, or a meeting, or even just trying to watch a movie... I start to feel this intense pressure inside my body. It's like I just need to get up, or shift around in my seat, or at least do something with my hands. If I can't move, it honestly feels like I'm going to crawl out of my skin.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others mid-sentence or blurting out answers before someone finishes asking a question?

Yeah, I do that a lot. Um, especially in conversations or, like, those job interviews I mentioned. I'll just jump in before the other person is even done talking. It's like I think I already know where they're going with the question, so I just blurt it out. But then half the time, I realize I answered the wrong question entirely, or I just completely cut them off. It's really frustrating.

Would you say this restlessness and impulsivity happen fairly consistently across different areas of your life—like at home, at work, and in social situations—or is it mostly limited to certain settings?

Yeah, it's pretty much everywhere. Um, I haven't really noticed it being limited to just one specific setting. Whether I'm at home, out with friends, or, you know, trying to do something professional like the interviews I mentioned... it's just kind of always there. It definitely happens across the board.
